steps.text: Maria is on her couch. She sees a pretty house on Zillow. She taps a button. Now you get a new lead.
Zillow and Realtor.com are big home search sites. People look at homes for sale there. Most of your leads come from them.

cards.back: A button. The lead wants to ask about a home.
A button. The lead wants to see the home.
A person who asked about a home.
A visit to see the home inside.

steps.q: What did your lead just do?
options: Tapped a button on a home they like
steps.why: They asked about one home. They did not buy yet.

steps.text: They just asked for help. They may have asked other agents too. The first kind, helpful caller usually wins.
Be first. Be kind. Be helpful.
steps.sub: The first helpful call usually wins the lead.

options: The lead may have asked other agents too
steps.why: The first helpful call usually wins.

steps.text: Open with the address of the home they looked at. Now they know why you are calling.

steps.line: Hi Maria, this is Sofia with Dana Lee's team. This call may be recorded. You asked about 12 Oak Street, right?

options.text: Hi Maria! Do you want to buy a home?
options.why: Too sudden. She does not know why you called.

options.text: Hi Maria, it's Sofia with Dana Lee's team. You asked about 12 Oak Street?
options.why: The address tells her why you called.

options.text: Hi, I am calling from a real estate company.
options.why: Not clear. Say the home's address.

steps.sub: It tells the lead why you are calling.

steps.text: Ask about that home first. "What did you like about it?" Then do A.L.M. That means Appointment, Location, Motivation.

items: Say your name and your team
Say the call may be recorded
Do A.L.M. and offer a tour time

cards.back: They want to see the home. Offer a time now.
They want to know one thing. Help, then offer a tour.
They are early. Be kind and follow up.

steps.says: Yes, I want to see that house.

options.text: OK, I will email you some info.
options.why: She asked for a tour. Offer a time now.

options.text: Great! The agent will call you some day.
options.why: "Some day" is not a plan. Offer two times.

options.text: Great! Would Saturday at 11 or 2 work better?
options.why: Two choices make it easy to say yes.

steps.line: Would Saturday at 11 or 2 work better to see the home?

steps.says: Does that house have a garage?

options.text: Good question. I will ask the agent. Want to see it Saturday?
options.why: You helped. Then you offered a tour.

options.text: I'm not sure. I think so.

options.why: You can still help. Ask the agent for them.

options.text: OK, sorry to bother you. Bye.
options.why: You gave up too fast. Many buyers start this way.

options.text: No problem! Many people start that way. What did you like about that home?
options.why: Kind and calm. You kept the talk going.

options.text: You should buy now. Prices will go up.
options.why: Never push. Never talk about prices.

steps.text: Many leads are early. They are just looking. That is OK. Be kind. Follow up later.

steps.q: A lead says, "Maybe I will buy next year." What do you do?
options: Be kind, take notes and follow up
steps.why: Early leads can buy later. Stay friendly.

steps.q: Where do you write about each call?
steps.why: Every call gets a note in Follow Up Boss. Your leads live there.

steps.text: You did it! You can open a Zillow or Realtor.com call the right way.

quiz.q: What did a Zillow or Realtor.com lead just do?
options: Tapped a button about a home
quiz.explain: They tapped "Contact agent" or "Request a tour".

quiz.q: How do you show the lead why you called?
quiz.explain: The address tells the lead why you called.

options: The first helpful call usually wins
quiz.explain: The lead may have asked other agents too.

quiz.q: A lead wants a tour. What do you do?
quiz.explain: Ask, "Would Saturday at 11 or 2 work better?"

quiz.q: A lead is just looking. What do you do?
quiz.explain: Early lookers are normal. Many buy later.
